reference.title: Smith Bench Press
reference.listing: Video (title from the catalog listing; the page itself was not read from this environment)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace as you lower the bar, hold it through the touch, breathe out as you press it up.
breathing.cadence: About 2.0 s down, 0.3 s touch, 1.2 s up

prescription.tempo: 2-0-1-0 (2 s down, no pause, 1 s up)
prescription.load: Load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can press for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, about RPE 7-9).
prescription.progression: Add reps up to the top of the range, then add 1.25-2.5 kg.

cues.text: Bench square under the bar so it lands on the middle of the chest. Feet planted, glutes and upper back on the bench, shoulder blades pinched back and down. Grip overhand about one and a half shoulder widths apart, then turn the bar off the pegs.
Breathe in and lower the bar straight down the rails to the middle of the chest, elbows about 45-60 degrees from your sides.
Touch the chest lightly, no bounce; shoulder blades stay pinned, glutes stay on the bench.
Breathe out and press the bar straight up the rails until the arms are straight.
Re-brace with straight arms and go again; after the last rep, turn the bar back onto the pegs.

mistakes.mistake: Bench in the wrong place, so the bar comes down on the neck or the belly
mistakes.fix: Lie down and check the bar lines up with the middle of the chest before loading it.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flared straight out at 90 degrees (a "T")
mistakes.fix: Tuck the elbows to about 45-60 degrees.

mistakes.mistake: Bouncing the bar off the chest
mistakes.fix: Lower under control and touch lightly before pressing.
Keep the glutes on the bench and drive through the feet.

mistakes.mistake: Wrists bent back under the bar
mistakes.fix: Stack the bar over the heel of the palm, wrist and forearm.

kinematics.peak: Glutes on the seat, upper back and head on the pad (rig shapes)
kinematics.norm: Flat (0 degrees). The middle and lower parts of the pectoralis major were most active on a flat bench (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020)

kinematics.setup: 78 cm between the bar grips (≈2.0x the shoulder-joint width)
kinematics.norm: About 1.5 times shoulder width is a common middle grip; wider grips shortened the bar travel and changed muscle emphasis only slightly (Saeterbakken 2021)

kinematics.setup: ≈8° at the top (arms straight, not locked)
kinematics.peak: ≈123° with the bar on the chest
kinematics.norm: Arms straight but not locked at the top; elbows at roughly 90-110 degrees with the bar on the chest (clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Elbow flare (upper arm from the trunk)
kinematics.setup: Arms reaching up to the bar
kinematics.peak: ≈54° from the trunk at the bottom; upper arms ≈43° below the back plane
kinematics.norm: About 45-60 degrees from the body at the bottom, not a 90-degree "T" (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Vertical rails 10 cm toward the feet from the shoulder joints; top 58.1 cm above the bench
kinematics.peak: Bottom on the middle of the chest, 35.8 cm of travel
kinematics.norm: Fixed by the rails (vertical here), so the bar touches the middle of the chest and returns along the same line; chest activity was similar on the Smith machine, free barbell and dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2011)
Feet flat on the floor with the knees bent about 90 degrees, like the bench set-up in Solstad 2020

kinematics.peak: 2 s down, 0.3 s touch, 1.2 s up, 0.7 s at the top
kinematics.norm: Controlled: about 2 s down and 1-2 s up (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020 used 2 s down and 2 s up)

cautions: Set the safety stops just below chest height before the first rep, so the bar can be left on them if you get stuck.
Practise turning the bar on and off the pegs with an empty bar first.
Position the bench so the bar lands on the middle of the chest, not the neck.
Shoulder pain: shorten the range at the bottom or narrow the grip slightly until it settles (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: a slightly narrower grip with the elbows tucked a little more, or a dumbbell press.
Lower back arching too much: feet on a low step or on the end of the bench.
progressions: Pause bench press (1-2 s on the chest).

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main pusher: horizontal adduction and flexion of the upper arm. On a flat bench the middle (sternal) and lower (costal) fibres were most active (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020), and pectoralis activity was similar for barbell, dumbbell and Smith machine presses (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Main pusher: horizontal adduction and flexion of the upper arm. On a flat bench the middle (sternal) and lower (costal) fibres were most active (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020), and pectoralis activity was similar for barbell, dumbbell and Smith machine presses (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Flexes the shoulder with the chest; the rails take over most of the balancing work (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Flexes the shoulder with the chest; the rails take over most of the balancing work (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straighten the elbows in the top half of the press.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straighten the elbows in the top half of the press.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Holds the shoulder blades against the rib cage as the bar is pressed.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Holds the shoulder blades against the rib cage as the bar is pressed.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: A minor stabiliser; less active on the Smith machine than with dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: A minor stabiliser; less active on the Smith machine than with dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm in the socket (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm in the socket (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the shoulder blades pinned back and down on the bench.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Keep the shoulder blades pinned back and down on the bench.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the ribs down and the pelvis on the bench.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Help control the bar on the way down and keep the upper back tight.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Help control the bar on the way down and keep the upper back tight.

phases.label: Bar touches the middle of the chest

guides.label: Elbows bent to bring the bar to the chest
